children: “Facilities and incentives”
“便利条件与激励”
[Freedom for the rich]
〔富人的自由〕
P. T. Harvest International [“Indonesia’s leading business development firm”]: So what facilities and incentives can foreign investors expect should they want to invest in South Kalimantan?
P. T. Harvest International 公司〔“印尼领先的商业发展公司”〕：
那么，如果外国投资者想在南加里曼丹投资，可以期待什么样的便利条件与激励？
Governor H. M. Sjachriel Darham:

We will facilitate permits and settle land disputes. The provincial government will be proactive in settling problems. The provincial government will also help the company promote itself with the local people.
H. M. 夏赫里尔·达拉姆省长：
我们将协助办理许可，并解决土地纠纷。省政府将主动解决问题。省政府还将帮助公司向当地人宣传自身。
Harvest:
How is the security situation?
Harvest：
安全形势如何？
Gov. Sjachriel:

Security is very good. South Kalimantan was not even affected by the ethnic conflicts that took place in Central Kalimantan, even though it’s right next door. South Kalimantan has been able to maintain security and is considered the safest region in Indonesia, according to the central government.
夏赫里尔省长：
安全非常好。南加里曼丹甚至没有受到中加里曼丹族群冲突的影响，尽管它就在旁边。南加里曼丹能够维持安全，据中央政府说，被认为是印尼最安全的地区。
Harvest:
If, for instance, a foreign company were to experience problems, would you and your office be willing to help?
Harvest：
比如，如果一家外国公司遇到问题，您和您的办公室愿意帮忙吗？
Gov. Sjachriel:

We will be glad to assist. We admit that some investors in South Kalimantan have experienced problems with claims of land ownership by local people. We have recommended the President issue a Presidential Decree that, in the event of such claims, the people must submit their legal suits against the central government, the provincial government, or the district government and not against the company or investors concerned. We are still waiting for such a policy. It is not proper to sue the businessmen or investors in such case. (Garuda 2002: 54–55)

The post-New Order period has been a bundle of contradictions. Political life has revived in cities and towns. Meanwhile, a new level of chaos and violence has torn up much of the countryside. U.S.-led global war has encouraged a return of military rule, while military crimes of all sorts are reported everywhere. The sad destruction of the forests by Suharto’s cronies is discussed widely; at the same time, illegal resource extraction has blossomed beyond Suharto’s dreams. Corruption is criticized even as it proliferates everywhere. International conservation groups gain clout in the environmental field as Indonesia becomes poorer and more dependent: and this just at the moment radical national environmentalists worked so hard to achieve.
夏赫里尔省长：
我们乐意协助。我们承认，南加里曼丹一些投资者遇到过当地人主张土地所有权的问题。我们已建议总统发布总统令：若出现此类主张，人民必须对中央政府、省政府或县政府提起法律诉讼，而不是对涉事公司或投资者。我们仍在等待这样的政策。在这种情况下起诉商人或投资者是不恰当的。（Garuda 2002: 54–55）

新秩序后时期是一团矛盾。城市和城镇的政治生活已经复兴。与此同时，新的混乱和暴力撕裂了大部分乡村。美国领导的全球战争鼓励军事统治回归，同时各地都有各种军事犯罪的报道。苏哈托亲信对森林的可悲破坏被广泛讨论；与此同时，非法资源开采的繁荣超出苏哈托的梦想。腐败受到批评，却在各地蔓延。随着印尼变得更贫穷、更依赖他人，国际保护团体在环境领域获得影响力：而这恰恰发生在激进的全国环保主义者如此努力希望促成的时刻。

It is in this context that enforcement has become the dominant trope in conservation for the international organizations. Enough about community empowerment, they say: Let’s get the criminals. As one foreign consultant explained, “true reform demands law, order and governance in natural-resource management” (Ivereigh 2003: 29). But how shall we create order? From the international perspective, there is only one proven formula: the recognition of the exclusive rights of national and international elites to claim valuable things. We call these rights “property.”
在这种背景下，执法已成为国际组织保护工作的主导修辞。他们说，社群赋权谈够了：让我们抓罪犯。正如一位外国顾问所解释的，“真正的改革要求自然资源管理中的法律、秩序和治理”（Ivereigh 2003: 29）。但我们如何创造秩序？从国际视角看，只有一种被证明有效的公式：承认国内和国际精英对有价值之物的排他性权利。我们把这些权利称为“财产”。

My mother sends me The Nature Conservancy’s latest magazine because it contains an article on saving wild orangutans in Kalimantan (Ivereigh 2003). Orangutans are good-looking primates with their red shaggy hair and mobile faces. Unfortunately for their future, they live in lowland tropical rainforests, eating fruits, insects, leaves, and other plant material. They reproduce slowly (a female raises at most four offspring), and they require large tracts of solitary space. As the forest is felled and fragmented, orangutans suffer and die. Survivors are shot or captured for the illegal pet trade, particularly by loggers. The conservationists who inform the article are not at all optimistic that any will survive in the wild.

母亲寄给我大自然保护协会的最新杂志，因为里面有一篇关于拯救加里曼丹野生红毛猩猩的文章（Ivereigh 2003）。猩猩是长得好看的灵长类，有着红色蓬乱的毛发和富有表情的脸。对它们的未来而言，不幸的是，它们生活在低地热带雨林，吃果实、昆虫、树叶和其他植物材料。它们繁殖缓慢（一只雌性最多养育四个后代），需要大片独处空间。随着森林被砍伐和破碎化，猩猩受苦并死亡。幸存者被枪杀或捕获用于非法宠物贸易，尤其是被伐木者。为文章提供信息的保护主义者对任何猩猩能在野外存活一点也不乐观。

Privileged Americans, raised with stuffed animals and fuzzy pets, like big mammals, and it makes good sense to tell the story of Kalimantan’s forests to a U.S. audience through orangutans. These American preferences can be a conservation nightmare, as when people insist on the well-being of every animal even when that animal is destroying a multispecies habitat. But the synergies between wild orangutans and rainforests are only positive ones. It is impossible to protect wild orangutans without protecting forest. Orangutans don’t even steal crops or attack people; they only want to be left alone. I am willing to risk sneers about “charismatic megafauna” to support the campaign for wild orangutans; to work for wild orangutans is to work for the forest. However, the implications for the indigenous people who have lived longest with the forest are more ambiguous. Forest-dwelling peoples ought to benefit from forest protection programs. However, it is also possible to imagine conservation programs for orangutans that further rip off and displace indigenous people—even while protecting a certain amount of their socially nurtured forest. It is up to organizations such as The Nature Conservancy to determine the course. Will conservation work for or against forest-dwelling communities? Who will be conservation’s allies?
校注19

伴着毛绒玩具和毛茸茸宠物长大的特权美国人喜欢大型哺乳动物，用猩猩向美国受众讲述加里曼丹森林的故事很合理。这些美国偏好可能成为保护噩梦，例如当人们坚持每一只动物的福祉，即使那只动物正在破坏多物种栖息地。但野生猩猩与雨林之间的协同效应只有正面的。不保护森林就不可能保护野生猩猩。猩猩甚至不偷庄稼，也不攻击人；它们只想不被打扰。我愿意冒着被人嘲笑“魅力型大型动物”的风险，支持保护野生猩猩的运动；为野生猩猩工作就是为森林工作。然而，这对与森林共处最久的原住民意味着什么，则更为含混。森林居民本应受益于森林保护项目。然而，也可以想象为猩猩设计的保护项目进一步剥削和驱逐原住民——即使它保护了一定数量由社会培育的森林。方向取决于大自然保护协会等组织。保护将有利于还是不利于森林居民社群？谁将成为保护的盟友？
校注19

Among environmental organizations, The Nature Conservancy is best known for its deep commitments to capitalism and private property. Historically, the organization imagined its mission as buying up land to protect it from development. This strategy was expanded as the Conservancy was able to solicit the donation of private lands, which either themselves become conservation lands or allow the organization to buy more ecologically valuable patches. In the 1980s and 1990s, the organization grew exponentially, becoming the world’s richest environmental group (Ottaway and Stephens 2003a). The Conservancy became known for its corporate partnerships, which range from soliciting funds to urging environmental standards in exchange for the organization’s imprimatur. This issue of the magazine, for example, includes an article on how the Conservancy has benefited from the generosity of General Motors, including U.S.$23 million of grant money in the last ten years (Wilkonson 2003). Still, the heart of the Conservancy is the preservation of land through ownership.

在环保组织中，大自然保护协会以其对资本主义和私有财产的深刻承诺而闻名。历史上，该组织把自己的使命想象为买下土地以保护其免受开发。随着协会能够募集私人土地捐赠——这些土地或本身成为保护地，或使组织能够购买更多具有生态价值的地块——这一策略得到扩展。20世纪80和90年代，该组织指数式增长，成为世界上最富有的环保团体（Ottaway and Stephens 2003a）。协会以企业伙伴关系闻名，范围从募集资金到敦促企业遵守环境标准，并以协会的认可作为交换。例如，这一期杂志有一篇文章讲协会如何受益于通用汽车的慷慨，包括过去十年2300万美元的资助（Wilkonson 2003）。尽管如此，协会的核心仍然是通过所有权保护土地。

This is a strategy that depends on unquestioning confidence in private property and the political economy (e.g., law; contracts; inheritance; police protection; “interest” in several senses; transnational convertibility) that makes property worthwhile. In the United States, where this political economy is rather pervasive, it is arguably a worthwhile strategy, tapping the environmental consciousness of the landed elite and holding back the tide of destructive development. Despite their disagreements with the Conservancy’s corporate policies, many U.S. environmentalists express respect for the organization’s land acquisition programs. Outside of the United States it is difficult to be so sanguine. To promote private property and corporate rights in tropical rainforests is not just advocacy for the prevailing system of inequality; it introduces a new and terrible inequality, as it supports the expropriation of land and resources from the forest's old inhabitants. If worked through properly, land rights could protect forest communities; but of all the many international organizations promoting private property in Kalimantan, none, to my knowledge, have addressed the justice of a system in which forest residents, by definition, have no property. While “benefits” may be channeled to “local communities,” property is for elites.

这是一项依赖于对私有财产及使财产具有价值的政治经济体系（例如法律、合同、继承、警察保护、兼有利益、利息等多重含义的“interest”、跨国可兑换性）不加质疑的信心的策略。在美国，这种政治经济相当普遍，这可以说是一项有价值的策略，利用有地精英的环境意识，抵挡破坏性发展的浪潮。尽管与大自然保护协会的企业政策存在分歧，许多美国环保主义者对该组织的土地购置项目表示尊重。在美国之外，很难如此乐观。在热带雨林推广私有财产和企业权利，不只是倡导盛行不平等制度；它引入一种新的可怕不平等，因为它支持从森林原有居民手中征用土地和资源。如果处理得当，土地权可以保护森林社群；但在加里曼丹推广私有财产的众多国际组织中，据我所知，没有一个处理过这样一个制度的正义问题：森林居民按定义没有财产。尽管“利益”可能被输送给“当地社群”，财产是给精英的。

In Kalimantan, it was the Suharto regime that claimed the forests for the state, and then divided them up for the benefit of crony capitalism. Post-New Order legalities depend on this economy of theft. Companies want their fair share of the free lands created by decree; this is freedom for the rich. Some social democrats imagine the flood of immigrants, with their legal and illegal schemes, as evening out the score. But this view ignores those who already live there. From the perspective of old forest residents, legal and illegal schemes are not so different. Funded and authorized from common sources, their products find their way into common commercial pools. Legal and illegal exploiters combine forces to wrest their profits from the forest and those who depend upon it.

在加里曼丹，是苏哈托政权把森林收归国家所有，然后为裙带资本主义的利益进行分配。新秩序后的合法性依赖于这种盗窃经济。公司想要由法令变成可自由占取的土地中自己的一份；这是富人的自由。一些社会民主主义者想象移民洪流——带着他们的合法与非法计划——会扯平局面。但这种观点忽视了已经生活在那里的人。从森林原有居民的角度看，合法与非法计划差别不大。它们由共同来源资助和授权，其产品进入共同的商业流通渠道。合法与非法开采者联合力量，从森林及依赖森林者手中夺取利润。

Resource exploitation has indeed gotten out of control. But what should be done? The Nature Conservancy suggests that legally licensed corporations, the ones with national and international clout, are the answer. They argue that the forest can be best protected by working together with logging companies, who will patrol the forest because it is in their economic interest to exclude illegal loggers. In turn, they will offer these environmentally conscious companies the benefits of ecological certification. “Our task,” says the Conservancy’s Scott Stanley, “is to offer a packet of incentives so compelling that companies will actually implement certification” (Ivereigh 2003: 30).
资源开采确实已经失控。但应该做什么？大自然保护协会提出，拥有国内和国际影响力的合法许可公司就是答案。他们论证说，与伐木公司合作最能保护森林，伐木公司会巡逻森林，因为排除非法伐木者符合其经济利益。作为回报，他们将向这些有环境意识的公司提供生态认证的好处。“我们的任务，”大自然保护协会的斯科特·斯坦利说，“是提供一揽子极具吸引力的激励，使公司真正实施认证”（Ivereigh 2003: 30）。

Working together with wood retailers such as Home Depot, Lowe’s, and IKEA, the Conservancy’s certification program would give corporate loggers better prices. Stanley tells them, “We’re here to help you improve markets. We’re here to make things easier for you” (ibid.: 30). Certification could increase market prices for Indonesian wood, thus offering the companies better conditions. According to the article, a number of Indonesian companies are already interested in the program.
与家得宝、劳氏和宜家等木材零售商合作，协会的认证项目会给企业伐木者更好的价格。斯坦利告诉他们：“我们来这里是为了帮助你们改善市场。我们来这里是为了让你们的事更容易”（同上：30）。认证可以提高印尼木材的市场价格，从而为公司提供更好的条件。据文章称，一些印尼公司已经对该项目感兴趣。

In contrast, the Conservancy feels that parks and nature reserves are unhelpful in the current situation. Stanley explains: “Ironically it would be counterproductive to push for a protected area. It takes years to get a park approved, and, as we’ve seen in other areas, timber companies generally use that time to log as intensively as possible. Besides that, Indonesia can’t afford to protect the parks it has now” (ibid.: 25). The article goes on to explain that police and government officials are only interested in bribes. The author comments: “So wide is the web of corruption that those officials who do prosecute illegal loggers may find themselves ostracized or threatened. Few rise to meet the challenge, especially given Indonesia’s conflicting laws and the generally dismal prospects for conviction” (ibid.: 26). It is interesting that the Conservancy, which, reasonably enough, criticizes government enforcers, continues to have such faith in the private enforcers of the corporate economy. What makes them think these private militias will be any different? It is a faith that can only be interpreted as a deep, ideological conviction: privatization is always better. Even after the slew of privatization scandals that have bankrupted public funds in the United States in the preceding few years, privatization wears a halo.

相比之下，协会认为公园和自然保护区在当前情况下无济于事。斯坦利解释说：“讽刺的是，推动建立一个保护区会适得其反。让一个公园获批需要数年时间，而正如我们在其他地区看到的，木材公司通常利用那段时间尽可能密集地伐木。此外，印尼负担不起保护现有公园的费用”（同上：25）。文章接着解释，警察和政府官员只对贿赂感兴趣。作者评论说：“腐败网络如此之广，以至于那些确实起诉非法伐木者的官员可能会发现自己被排斥或受到威胁。很少有人挺身迎接挑战，尤其是考虑到印尼相互矛盾的法律和普遍黯淡的定罪前景”（同上：26）。有趣的是，协会相当合理地批评政府执法者，却继续对企业经济的私人执法者抱有这样的信心。是什么让他们认为这些私人武装会有所不同？这种信心只能被解释为一种深刻的意识形态信念：私有化总是更好。即使在前几年一系列私有化丑闻使美国公共资金破产之后，私有化仍戴着光环。

Certification can be a good thing. I am pleased to see the article mention the independent and nonprofit Forest Stewardship Council (FSC), which offers the most responsible certification program of which I know. The FSC requires that certification address land tenure and indigenous rights as well as forest sustainability. If there is going to be corporate logging—and I’m sure there is—it ought to have some framework of responsibility. Yet one independent assessment has concluded that, because of land expropriation, “certification to FSC standards in Indonesia is currently not possible” (Colchester et al. 2003: 270). Indonesian environmentalists and indigenous leaders have called for a moratorium on certification (Lawrence et al. 2003).

认证可以是好事。我高兴地看到文章提到独立非营利的森林管理委员会（FSC），它提供了我所知最负责任的认证项目。FSC 要求认证涉及土地保有权和原住民权利以及森林可持续性。如果要有企业伐木——我相信会有——它应当有某种责任框架。然而，一份独立评估得出结论，由于土地征用，“目前在印尼不可能达到 FSC 标准的认证”（Colchester et al. 2003: 270）。印尼环保主义者和原住民领袖呼吁暂停认证（Lawrence et al. 2003）。
Yet Indonesian environmentalists and indigenous leaders are entirely missing from the article.

The article describes a landscape populated only by foreign experts, on the one hand, and Indonesian poachers and loggers, on the other. (One orangutan survey leader is Indonesian, but the article never lets us hear from him.) The result is that we imagine an imperially mandated nature, protected for the appreciation of international elites. Indigenous communities are given a symbolic nod: a one-sentence assurance that the Conservancy will “increase the benefits of local communities from legitimate timber concessions” (Ivereigh 2003: 30) and a touristic photograph. The latter is confusingly captioned: “Meanwhile, generations of Punan people (above) have lived in and relied on the forest; their culture depends on its survival—and perhaps its on theirs” (ibid.: 29). If the Punan are necessary to the forest, why aren’t they consulted in the article? Why weren’t they invited to the certification workshop, which included only industry leaders and conservation authorities? And where are Indonesian activists, democrats, community spokespeople, and environmental scientists? Are these omissions just aesthetic tactics to draw the U.S. audience of the magazine, or do they reflect the Conservancy’s policy? One fears the latter. One fears that the Conservancy’s deep faith in capitalism and private property has overridden their ability to assess the political situation. They have chosen allies, but not those who can tell them about the social world of the forest. They will have to rely on shooting poachers—with all the terrible consequences of that decision.
然而，印尼环保主义者和原住民领袖在文章中完全缺席。

文章描绘的地景，一边只有外国专家，另一边只有印尼偷猎者和伐木者。（一位猩猩调查负责人是印尼人，但文章从未让我们听到他的声音。）结果是，我们想象一种由帝国授权的自然，为国际精英的欣赏而保护。原住民社群只得到象征性点头：一句保证大自然保护协会将“增加当地社群从合法的伐木特许区中获得的利益”（Ivereigh 2003: 30），以及一张旅游照片。后者的说明文字令人困惑：“与此同时，世世代代的普南人（上图）生活在森林中并依赖森林；他们的文化依赖森林的存续——也许森林也依赖他们”（同上：29）。如果普南人对森林是必要的，为什么文章中不咨询他们？为什么不邀请他们参加只包括行业领袖和保护当局的认证工作坊？印尼活动家、民主派、社群发言人和环境科学家又在哪里？这些省略只是吸引杂志美国受众的审美策略，还是反映了协会的政策？令人担心的是后者。令人担心的是，协会对资本主义和私有财产的深刻信仰压倒了其评估政治局势的能力。他们选择了盟友，但不是那些能告诉他们森林社会世界的人。他们将不得不依赖射杀偷猎者——以及那个决定的所有可怕后果。

I go online to find out more about The Nature Conservancy's Indonesia projects. I know they have worked with communities in other areas of Indonesia, such as Lore Lindu National Park. There, researcher Tania Li (2000) found that the Conservancy fetishized one set of local villagers as traditional tribesmen, although they were no different than farmers throughout the region. Li charges that the Conservancy has ignored the larger context of social justice in Indonesia. Given the erasure of social process in the portrayals of nature I find, I understand this worry in a new way. The Conservancy’s language of community participation is bland and almost insulting: “Through a systematic and user-friendly process that uses cards, poster boards and smiley faces rather than computers and complex data sheets, village members are asked to identify what they value most about the park” (Nature Conservancy 2001). Are conservationists sales representatives with no ability to participate in conversation? I find an online account of the orangutan project that offers a new bit of information: the researchers have trained “local villagers, including a number of indigenous and forest-dependent Punan Dayaks” to conduct the orangutan survey (Nature Conservancy 2002). Perhaps there is more to say about local participation that doesn’t come through in these accounts. Why are the writers so coy?

我上网查找更多关于大自然保护协会印尼项目的信息。我知道他们曾在印尼其他地区与社群合作，例如洛雷林杜国家公园。在那里，研究者 Tania Li（2000）发现，协会将一群当地村民奉为传统部落民的典范，尽管他们与整个地区的农民没有不同。Li 指出协会忽视了印尼社会正义的更大语境。鉴于我在自然描绘中发现的社会过程抹除，我以新的方式理解这种担忧。协会关于社群参与的语言平淡得几乎侮辱人：“通过一个使用卡片、海报板和笑脸图标的系统而用户友好的过程，而不是电脑和复杂的数据表，要求村庄成员找出他们最看重公园的什么”（Nature Conservancy 2001）。保护主义者难道是没有参与对话能力的销售代表吗？我在网上找到一份关于猩猩项目的叙述，提供了新的信息：研究人员培训了“当地村民，包括一些原住民和依赖森林的普南达雅克人”进行猩猩调查（Nature Conservancy 2002）。也许关于当地参与还有更多可说的，只是没有在这些叙述中体现出来。为什么作者们如此讳莫如深？

Then I find a rather different source. The issue of the magazine I am reading, with its gorgeous nature scenes, must have arrived in subscribers’ mailboxes just as The Washington Post published a major expose of the Conservancy’s bad practices (Ottaway and Stephens 2003a, 2003b, 2003c).

The reporters detail the influence of corporate moguls on the Conservancy’s environmental policies, the effects of profit-making on species protection, and the practice of selling conservation land cheaply to Conservancy officials for their summer homes. The Conservancy, they tell us, has refused to take positions on issues such as global warming and drilling in Alaska’s Arctic National Wildlife Refuge to avoid criticizing their corporate sponsors. In one case, the Conservancy sponsored oil drilling on conservation land donated to protect endangered birds; bird numbers dwindled. The series raises the question of whether capitalist accumulation and conservation objectives can work together harmoniously—in the United States as well as beyond. Even in the United States, acquisition is not politically neutral. It is a struggle for freedom—for the rich.
然后我找到一个相当不同的来源。我正在阅读的这期杂志满是绚丽自然场景，它一定是在《华盛顿邮报》发表关于协会不良做法的大型揭露报道时，刚好送进订户邮箱的（Ottaway and Stephens 2003a, 2003b, 2003c）。

记者详细披露了企业巨头对协会环境政策的影响、营利对物种保护的影响，以及把保护地廉价卖给协会官员作避暑别墅的做法。他们告诉我们，协会拒绝就全球变暖和阿拉斯加北极国家野生动物保护区钻探等问题表明立场，以免批评其企业赞助者。在一个案例中，协会赞助在捐赠用于保护濒危鸟类的保护地上进行石油钻探；鸟类数量减少。这组报道提出一个问题：资本主义积累与保护目标能否和谐共存——在美国以及在别处。即使在美国，土地购置也不是政治中立的。这是一场争取自由的斗争——富人的自由。

en: The Indonesian Minister of the Environment is quoted, explaining the omission of other Indonesian agendas by suggesting that what Indonesians need most is enforcement-oriented foreign intervention: “Combating unlawful logging should top the list of developed countries’ priorities in line with their commitment to conserve tropical forests” (Ivereigh 2003: 29).
zh: 文中引用了印尼环境部长的话，为其他印尼议程被省略作解释，提出印尼人最需要的是以执法为导向的外国干预：“打击非法伐木应列在发达国家优先事项之首，以符合其保护热带森林的承诺”（Ivereigh 2003: 29）。

en: Worse yet, they describe the certification program in misleading rhetoric: “To protect orangutan habitat, The Nature Conservancy is facilitating the development and implementation of a locally derived model for collaborative management that will create incentives necessary to gain support from forest-dependent communities, forest industry, and the local and provincial government” (The Nature Conservancy 2002). What could this possibly mean, and why don’t they tell us?
zh: 更糟的是，他们用误导性的修辞描述认证项目：“为了保护红毛猩猩栖息地，大自然保护协会正在推动制定和实施一种源自当地的协作管理模式，该模式将创造必要的激励，以赢得依赖森林的社群、林业产业以及地方和省级政府的支持”（The Nature Conservancy 2002）。这究竟可能是什么意思？他们为什么不告诉我们？

en: Follow-up articles on a congressional investigation and the Conservancy's response are, respectively, Stephens (2003) and Stephens and Ottaway (2003).
zh: 关于国会调查及大自然保护协会回应的后续文章，分别见 Stephens（2003）和 Stephens and Ottaway（2003）。

en: Meanwhile, other alliances and tactics have been in play. WALHI, AMAN (The Indigenous People’s Alliance of the Archipelago), and the U.S.-based Rainforest Action Network (RAN) have called on U.S. firms to stop buying Indonesian wood. RAN has singled out The Conservancy’s partner, Home Depot, for “good promises, bad results.” See Rainforest Action Network (2003).
zh: 与此同时，其他联盟和策略也一直在发挥作用。WALHI、AMAN（群岛原住民联盟）以及总部位于美国的雨林行动网络（RAN）呼吁美国公司停止购买印尼木材。RAN 特别点名大自然保护协会的合作伙伴 家得宝（Home Depot），指其“承诺很好，结果糟糕”。见 Rainforest Action Network（2003）。
